svg.aria-label: City Investigator. Evidence, not guesses: a resident's street photo, checked against New York City's public records. Built with Meta's SAM 3.1 and Muse Spark 1.3. Three numbered panels. 1, Inputs and evidence: an illustrated Brooklyn rowhouse street with a sidewalk shed and a flooded corner. Photo plus question: Is flooding a recurring problem here? Faces and plates blurred. SAM 3.1, a Meta model, segments the same scene with colored masks on the shed and water. Public records: 311 complaints, permits, sensors (FloodNet), and the city's flood model, shown as stacked map layers. Evidence store and its blind spots. A, Records against reality: photo vs. records; agree, disagree, gap. Example: permit valid, no shed in view. 2, Reasoning: Muse Spark 1.3, a Meta model and agent with tools: look again with SAM 3.1 in a two-way loop, read records, search records, building records. Labeled claims: Observed, Recorded, Modeled, Inferred, No coverage, Proposal. B, Evidence, not guesses: a claim checker. No evidence of the right kind: dropped. Only checked claims pass to the answer. A dashed repair loop returns to Muse Spark. C, Grounded proposals feed into the agent and checker: real channels (311, Brooklyn Community Board 6, DEP Green Infrastructure); precedents (how similar reports ended across the district); at most one idea from elsewhere. No promises. 3, What the resident sees: Answer with claims linked to a map and a timeline. D, Needs at stake: Protection, Comfort, Enjoyment (Jan Gehl's criteria). E, An honest 3D twin: 3D city in Valdrada, third-party, MIT, a visualization, not evidence or a Meta model. Before: evidence in place, flood water and permitted sheds. After: proposals at real scale; rain gardens added, the water remains. The gardens hold only a small share of the water. District overview: 26 places, 8 where records and photo disagree. Bottom picture pipeline: A street photo and a question; NYC public records; SAM 3.1 + Muse Spark 1.3; Checked, labeled claims; Residents act through real channels. THE FIVE IDEAS legend repeats A through E. Data: NYC Open Data · FloodNet · NYC Stormwater Flood Maps · Mapillary | 3D: Valdrada (MIT). Pictures are AI-generated illustrations, not evidence.
